## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-1-2"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox odv-am-pending">Drawn in Figma by the Open DS anatomy plugin; the image is not exported yet.</span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">1</i><i class="odv-am-n">2</i><b>Track and range</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="What holds this?">Containment</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="What state is it in?">Meaning</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Color · Which color roles does it need? → Those and brand accents</div><div class="odv-am-why">Each brand brings its own accent ramp.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Shape · What should control corners say? → Rounded</div><div class="odv-am-why">Rounded by default; each brand sets its own corner.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.surface.sunken</code><span>→</span><code>track.background</code><span class="odv-am-val">#F1F5F9 · dark #1E293B</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">A recessed fill, a step below content.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.100, a step below content (1.1:1 on surface.default), so table headers and wells read as recessed.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.100, a step below content (1.22:1 on surface.default), so table headers and wells read as recessed.</div><div><b>Shares the step with</b> surface.highlight, action.secondary.hover, disabled.surface. Changing this pick moves only what reads color.surface.sunken.</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>radius.round</code><span>→</span><code>track.radius</code><span class="odv-am-val">9999px</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> radius.full</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.action.primary</code><span>→</span><code>range.background</code><span class="odv-am-val">#0F766E · dark #7FCFC6</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">The one main action in a view.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> teal.light.600: the primary action's fill; its label reads, 5.47:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div><div><b>Dark</b> teal.dark.600: the primary action's fill; its label reads, 9.9:1, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div><div><b>Shares the step with</b> border.focus, border.selected, category.1. Changing this pick moves only what reads color.action.primary.</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `slider`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy multi-brand slider`
